h: Gavin, Stacey and a box of good food
p: Barry is forever linked with Gavin and Stacey, the much-loved sitcom set and filmed in the town, and fans still come to spot locations around Barry Island. So if you're making a day of it, a Goodsheds lunch followed by a wander round the island is a natural pairing. It's the sort of trip that ticks off food, telly nostalgia and sea air in one go.

Goodsheds sits close to Barry Docks station, which makes it easy to reach on the train from Cardiff without worrying about parking. Once you're there, it's a walk-around, try-a-bit kind of place. Have a look at what each trader is serving before committing, as the line-up of food and drink can change. Bring a bit of patience at busy times, especially weekend lunchtimes, when the most popular spots get queues.
Families with younger kids will find it relaxed enough to let them wander a little, and the setting, with its bright containers and old railway carriages, makes for a fun photo stop.

If you've still got energy afterwards, Porthkerry Country Park on the western edge of Barry has woodland, a pebble beach and an impressive Victorian railway viaduct striding across the valley. The Knap, with its pebbly beach and gardens, is another lovely spot for a stroll and a breath of sea air. Barry Island Pleasure Park is right there on the island too if the kids still have energy to burn, and the views back across the bay are lovely on a clear day.
